text.p: Portuguese bonds fell in line with other southern European markets after a report that European Commission officials have forecast Italy's budget deficit this year above the target level for entry into the single currency.
Dealers expected more falls in the absence of U.S. economic indicators to lift the gloom.

"The peripheral European markets are being hit again. Once more it looks like Italy won't meet the Maastricht criteria and the situation on the currency markets isn't great either. I think we'll see the downward trend continuing," said one trader.
The market was also weakened by the retreat of the escudo which fell sharply against a strong German mark.

Traders' views were mixed on the future direction of the currency, with some saying that the fundamentals pointed to a strengthening, while others felt the fluctuations of the past two days suggested a further weakening.
